memory_candidates.content: For a helper script invoked as a short-lived subprocess (e.g. task-lock.sh) that needs to record the PID of its long-lived CALLING session (not its own $$), use a bounded ancestor-walk (ps -o ppid=/comm= up to ~10 hops, stop at pid 1) looking for a process name match, with an explicit fallback chain (found -> ppid -> self) and a pid_source field recording which branch fired. Pair this with a floor constant on any liveness-based reap so a misresolved pid can only ever SHORTEN a wait, never incorrectly reap a live session.

When a new per-entity registry file is keyed by a globally-unique caller-generated id (e.g. session_id), no mkdir-exclusivity gate is needed for writes -- each writer touches only its own path, so a plain tmp-file-write-then-mv (the write_holder pattern) is already race-free. Reserve mkdir-exclusivity primitives for cases where multiple writers could contend for the SAME path.

Two-signal staleness for a reap/cleanup feature: evaluate a fast-but-fallible liveness check (e.g. kill -0 pid) FIRST but only let it shorten the wait below a floor constant (never let 'process confirmably alive' count as proof of liveness on its own); always fall through to a slower, more conservative heartbeat-age threshold as the real backstop. This makes an unreliable fast signal safe to use opportunistically.
